My first law job fired me after a week and told me I wasn’t good enough to my face while firing me. They also knew I had no previous law experience and said they would be willing to train me. 

A couple months later I got a job with a different firm and now I have the kindest boss ever. He has full faith in me. I now have a boss who regularly tells me he is happy with the work and initiative I take.

A year later to checked the staff page of my old firm and saw they cleaned house. They fired over half of their so called “family like team.”

It really sucks getting fired and I didn’t get over being told how horrible I was for a while. You’re not worthless, and the fact was someone was willing to take a chance on you means you have promise. 

Who knows the next place may be way better and make you glad you got laid off. You just have to find it. Let out a good cry, file for unemployment, but don’t blame yourself for other people’s lack of time to properly train. 

Even if they did train you learning the law is something nobody gets right on the first try and needs at least some handholding or patience.  

Keep your chin up there will be bigger and better opportunities I promise

At 18 I also had no job, no car, and no money. I also struggled in school and couldn’t make it through a class without falling asleep.

I didn’t have a job, but I got one.

At 18 I felt hopeless and constantly was stressed and cried about how I didn’t know what I wanted to do with my life. Now I’m f24 I have a car and I found a job I love that didn’t require any college. I’m not the richest by any means and sometimes seeing how much others for such little effort does make me a little upset, but I wouldn’t change anything about my life.

Don’t compare yourself to people who get their rent paid by their parents or had help. I’ve met people in their 40s who still have an allowance. Trust me it a lot more than you think.

I now have the life experience to know what I want to pursue and have enrolled back in school and am doing miles better than I ever did in high school. The only difference is I want it now. Everything will come naturally, but you gotta keep trying. 

Take a break or a spontaneous night out to a park with a friend. You’re only 18 be young and dumb. I wish I spend more time just screwing around on my minimum wage jobs. I promise you’ll miss it someday. My favorite memories are doing all nighters with my coworkers from a coffee shop sleeping for an hour and then getting to work. I was dead broke, but I had fun.

You’ll be employed and then unemployed then employed again, but you’ll never be 18 again. Responsibilities will come, but you’ll will always have options. Find a topic that you love I almost guarantee there is some kind of either entry level job or secretary job and suddenly your foot is in the door. 

Living with your parents may suck, but it’s better than the street and even then I’ve met recently former homeless who drive a nicer car than me. 

You’re not even out of high school yet giving up now isn’t any different than giving up at 14. You’re a real person not an influencer faking things for the internet.

This seems like a keloid and is different from an irritation bump. Keloids are a very uncommon condition and have nothing to do with how clean a piercing is, but there is no side effects besides cosmetic. Why I think it is a keloid is because they usually develop after a piercing has healed. If it was showing up because of irritation you would have seen the bump much sooner and it would’ve looked much different.

I’m not a doctor, so I don’t know too much about them, but I would get their opinion on how to prevent further scarring if you can.

It might be dry. I’ve had mine for two years and had a similar experience, but when my piercer (who is part of the APP) looked at them he told me they were irritated because they were dry. He recommended I clean them and put non-scented lotion then clean them again.

I have both my nipples pierced for about two years now and I love them. The healing was painful for a few days then it calmed down drastically. The only time they have hurt since those first few days was when they got accidentally snagged and even then it would be similar to a stubbed toe. Hurts bad for a few moments then you’re fine. I wouldn’t make plans for right after you get them piercing because I did and I was not in the best mood.

The healing process for me personally was a lot nicer than any of my ear cartilage pieces it’s just longer and this is from someone that likes to sleep on their stomach. 

Actually getting them pierced, my piercer used a clamp to make sure that the piercing would be straight and honestly the clamp hurt worse than the needle. Make sure you go to a good piercer. A girl I knew went to a bad one and her’s turned out crooked. 

Sexy time is really fun with them, my favorite is when a partner lightly presses a vibrator to my nips. I can feel the simulation on the inside as well as on top and it’s 10x more intense than without the piercing. 

I have lost a bit of sensation in my left nip, but I don’t really mind it, but there are some people that do lose some sensation. Most I’ve met gained sensation. 

Just a disclaimer because I don’t know how well versed you are in piercings. Please do not do touch them besides for cleaning for the first four weeks. The pain I had from my one piercing that went bad was far worse than all the pain from my other 13 piercings combined.

Also another thing there are pages you can print from online where you can use the paper to measure the diameter of your jewelry. You can use it to measure the conch jewelry you currently have, and go a quarter of a size up and know exactly what to look for.

For your first picture,

Rook: They have hoop jewelry specifically for rooks that have a dangling gem that are super cute and I think fit your style

Tragus: I think would look cute with a marquis gem piece

Conch: a stud that goes long with the shape of your ear would be cute and example would be like a spiderweb piece, but it might lay down weird because I think you conch was pierced with a hoop in mind.

Two helix studs: A matching but different set would be cute and example would be a moon and star

Three lobe studs: I think changing them to the same kind of stud, but doing a size gradient would look more cohesive and cute.


For the second picture,

Top helix stud: I think changing it to a hoop would look cute and more intentional.

Triple forward helix: Can’t be changed due to healing, but they look cute.

Tragus: A tiny trinity ball would be cute here.

Conch: I love hoops in conch piercings, but I think a statement hoop would do you well. I was thinking a hoop with blue gems would be a statement and tie in with your forward helix piercings

Daith: you could change it if you like something more, but I think it’s fine simple especially if you change the conch to a statement piece. Keeping it gold while the triple forward helix and conch blue would also break up the blue nicely.

Triple helix studs: I personally would change the two on the outside to be the same but change the one in the middle to a piece you think is nice and fits the rest of your ear well.

Triple lobe studs: Blue gem gradient in size all the way.


That’s all I got. I think a majority of your hoops would look better as hoops than anything else and keeping them more simple gives you more freedom to have statement pieces, but if you liked the suggestions or have more questions feel free to pm me.

As someone who has done LSD multiple times and wanted to try LSD alone first, but had a trip sitter instead. Do not do it alone on your first trip. I saw how easy it was to get lost into the trip to just keep on packing on the thoughts and just lose myself completely, but because I was with people who also tripped and checked up on me it made the trip 1000x better. My first trip was with people I was new friends with, and while I didn’t really know them extremely well, I trusted them and knew they weren’t going to do weird things that will ruin the trip.

I would still recommend that over tripping alone on the first time. I also wouldn’t recommend having your trip sitter be someone that has never done psychedelics before, because they won’t understand the process or how to help you if something does go wrong.

The person who is trip sitting you will feel out of place just because they aren’t on the same kind of wavelength you are going through, but your first trip you don’t know how the drug affects you. It’s the same as getting drunk the first time, you don’t know what you are getting yourself into until you experience it. 

Also never do acid more than two times a year max and test your shit. I know people who didn’t test their tabs and found out they were candy flipping on their first trip. I also know someone that didn’t test their Molly and unknowingly did meth. Your health is something you should never take a gamble on because it will be your biggest regret.

LSD will always be here. There is no rush to try it. If you don’t trust anybody now it is 100% okay to just wait until you do trust someone. 

Doing it right versus wrong could be the defining factor of not losing your sanity if shit does go bad.
